notes: MULTIPLE-WIVES CORRECTION (research 2026-07-04, resolving Martha Taber Hedger's parent-too-young flag re: son William, b.1728): this tree attaches all five of Peter's tree-listed children (William 1728, Thomas 1734, Mary Ann 1746, Margaret 1764, Thomas John n.d.) to a single wife, Martha Taber Hedger, married 'Bet 1746 and 1748.' Real records show Peter had at least three, probably four, wives -- an unidentified first wife, Ann Hanna Ellis, Martha Taber (widow Hedger), and Christian Fisher (widow Roe) -- and that the marriage date and children currently on this record are misattributed.

Source: the unpublished 'Cheesman Family' manuscript by Albert Stirling Adams (held at the Gloucester County NJ Historical Society; transcribed at https://www.longislandsurnames.com/getperson.php?personID=I0675&tree=Roe), which reproduces Peter's actual probated will (dated 19 Apr 1786, proved 25 Aug 1788, Gloucester Twp.) naming: third wife Christian (Fisher, widow Roe) -- 100 pounds, 'married about 7 years' (i.e. c.1781, matching the deed record below); sons Richard(4) and Thomas(4) Cheesman (the homestead/millworks, split between them); daughter Mary Ann(4) Jackson (5 shillings, having 'already' received 400 acres); daughter Deborah(4) Pierce (60 pounds, wife of Henry Pierce -- NOT in this tree at all); daughter Margaret(4) Pierce (10 pounds, wife of William Pierce); grandson Jacob(5) Williams (via an unlisted son/daughter John(4) Williams). No 'William' appears as a son in the will -- only as 'my brother William(3) Cheesman' (i.e. Peter's own brother, per Richard Cheesman's documented children, b. abt 1713 Hempstead, d. 1766 Gloucester Co. NJ -- a different birth year than this tree's 'son' William (1728-1773), so not a certain match, but raising real doubt that 'William Cheesman b.1728' belongs in Peter's family at all as opposed to a name/generation mix-up).

The manuscript itself flags exactly this tree's underlying problem, unprompted: 'Children of Peter (3) Cheesman: According to the dates listed, all children were born before his second marriage. If he married Ann (3) Ellis in 1746 as stated, then all the children were born before that date too. Who was the mother of his children.' Independent WikiTree profiles (Cheesman-112 Peter; Ellis-4456 Ann Hanna Ellis, b.16 Apr 1710 England, d.1759 Gloucester NJ, m. Peter 1732 Upton, Burlington NJ; Cheesman-113 Thomas b.1734; Cheseman-5 Mary Ann Jackson b.1746; Cheesman-110 Richard D Cheesman b.1749 d.1799) resolve the manuscript's own question for three of the five children: Thomas, Mary Ann, and the untracked Richard D are Ann Ellis's, not Martha's -- all three WikiTree profiles cross-link consistently and match this tree's exact birth/death dates for Thomas and Mary Ann.

A real 1781 land-deed reference in the Adams manuscript ('George Sennor... bought land, 80 acres, from Peter (3) and Martha (3) (Hedger) Cheesman in 1781') independently documents Martha Taber (widow Hedger, her actual first husband per her own WikiTree profile Taber-815) as Peter's wife late in his life, after Ann Ellis's 1759 death -- not in 1746-48 as currently recorded. William (b.1728) predates every attested wife/marriage date found (1732 or 1746 for Ann Ellis; undated but post-1759 for Martha), so his mother is either an unidentified true first wife, or he is a misfiled relative (see brother William, above) rather than a genuine 1728 child of Peter's at all.

New findings not reflected in this tree: son Richard D Cheesman (b.16 Oct 1749, d.3 Nov 1799, m. Rachel Williams) and daughter Deborah Cheesman Pierce (m. Henry Pierce) are real, will-documented children of Peter's, currently missing entirely. Not added as new person records in this pass (no id assigned, no independent confirmation of exact vitals beyond the will abstract) -- flagged for a future research pass. Full writeup: docs/research/ancestors/gen09-martha-taber-hedger-eliza-bolton-taber.md.
